headline: Iran says messages still being passed to US via intermediaries
dek: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Tehran has never left the negotiating table, messages are still being passed to the US via intermediaries, and the obstacle is Washington's insistence on unilateral demands, repeatedly phrased as 'complete surrender', which he said no Iranian…
sources: Associated Press Sunday roundup, carried by Business Standard/Manila Bulletin/DTNext; Baghaei interview with German broadcaster ARD
fault_line: Deal or 'finish it off': is Trump's Sunday denial a genuine off-ramp while messages still move through intermediaries, or just a pause before strikes after the Israeli election and US midterms?

sections.what_happened: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Tehran has never left the negotiating table, messages are still being passed to the US via intermediaries, and the obstacle is Washington's insistence on unilateral demands, repeatedly phrased as 'complete surrender', which he said no Iranian accepts; he denied any Iranian role in alleged operations against British air bases and called the Strait of Hormuz 'not safe', blaming US/Israeli use of the waterway for attacks on Iran. Asked about an attack on Iran, President Trump said: 'No. There will not be a strike today.' Separately in the same AP roundup, the ICRC has begun receiving lists again of Palestinian detainees from the West Bank and Gaza after the Israeli Supreme Court ordered the government to resume sharing them. AP also notes CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper flew over Hormuz asserting over 3,000 commercial vessels transited with US military support over six months -- a claimant figure, NOT a counted one: the latest IMF PortWatch snapshot (2026-10-24, STALE, lag 6 days) counted 4 Hormuz transits on 2026-10-18, 7-day average 3.7 vs a 2025 baseline of 85.5/day.
sections.what_verified: AP (T1) as the reporting family for the roundup; Times of Israel (T3) independently corroborates Trump's 'no strike today' quote from the White House gaggle. Business Standard, Manila Bulletin, DTNext and BastillePost carry the same AP story (syndication = 1 AP family, not additional families). Baghaei's ARD remarks are additionally carried by Anadolu (T3, STATE TR), Al Mayadeen and Press TV, but those chains report the same interview, not independent verification of its claims.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's 'today' denial is time-bounded to Sunday and says nothing about after the Israeli election (Oct 27) or US midterms (Nov 3); Bloomberg/Fox reporting already recorded at totw-20261026-0600-01 has Trump weighing deal vs 'finish it off' with decision time approaching. Baghaei's 'complete surrender' characterisation of US demands is Tehran's framing, unconfirmed by Washington in this roundup. CENTCOM's 3,000-vessel figure conflicts in kind with PortWatch's counted 4 transits on Oct 18: different metrics (escorted/support transits over six months vs daily counted transits) and the PortWatch count is stale.
sections.why_matters: Tehran says the messages never stopped -- but calls Washington's demand 'complete surrender', a phrase it says no Iranian will accept. Trump, in the same breath, says no strike 'today'. The word doing all the work is 'today'.
sections.context: Background: Iran says messages still being passed to US via intermediaries; Trump says no strike 'today'; ICRC detainee lists resume

totw_analysis: Our read: Tehran says the messages never stopped -- but calls Washington's demand 'complete surrender', a phrase it says no Iranian will accept. Trump, in the same breath, says no strike 'today'. The word doing all the work is 'today'. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deal or 'finish it off': is Trump's Sunday denial a genuine off-ramp while messages still move through intermediaries, or just a pause before strikes after the Israeli election and US midterms?
